inspection_summary: Inspected the whole hash-matched source and made a gap-free partition over all 1,551 logical lines under the validator's splitlines convention (the file has 1,517 newline-delimited records, with embedded form-feed page boundaries explaining the difference). The source supports generic semantic units about Weierstrass encoding, local-to-global quotient constraints, vanishing-order classification, blowups, and birational transition mechanisms. Novelty is unconfirmed because isolation intentionally prevents comparison with #44 or prior corpus units. Physical duality dictionaries, spectra, brane interpretations, and affine-symmetry conjectures are outside the generic mathematical evidence used here.

accepted_units.title: Weierstrass data turns a varying elliptic fiber into a global discriminant geometry
accepted_units.why_material: A family of cubic equations packages elliptic fibers by coefficient sections; quotienting parameter redundancies gives the moduli count, and the discriminant identifies where smooth fibers degenerate.
accepted_units.context_note: Retain parameter quotient and discriminant mechanism; exclude the subsequent physical identification of degeneration points.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Degrees, rescaling weights, and the discriminant are readable, but exact weighted-projective normalization and tentative duality claims must not be imported.

accepted_units.title: Local coefficient data globalizes only after enforcing homogeneity and quotient invariance
accepted_units.why_material: Promoting local parameters to sections over another base encodes a fibration, while degree and C-star invariance constraints force a twisted ruled-surface quotient rather than a naive product.
accepted_units.context_note: The zero-size-instanton story is motivation only; the generic move is compatibility of local models with global line-bundle weights.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense polynomial degrees, homogeneous partners, and quotient weights require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Orders of vanishing classify local fiber singularities and expose a resolution boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Computing vanishing orders of two coefficients and their discriminant maps local equations to Kodaira-Tate types; excessive discriminant order marks failure of the desired crepant Calabi-Yau resolution.
accepted_units.context_note: Use as a generic classification move, not as evidence for associated gauge groups.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The table is flattened; every threshold and equality convention needs PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Cohomological contributions decompose global invariants by base, fibers, and sections
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates divisor classes inherited from the base, extra reducible-fiber components, and sections, showing how distinct geometric sources contribute to total Hodge data.
accepted_units.context_note: Physical multiplet and anomaly formulas are supporting context, not the generic unit target.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Hodge indices and rank formulas are legible but tied to assumptions of an elliptic Calabi-Yau with section.

accepted_units.title: Global canonical constraints sharply restrict admissible fibration bases
accepted_units.why_material: Resolving allowed base singularities and imposing the Calabi-Yau condition reduces possible bases to a short birational list, with holomorphic forms separating exceptional higher-symmetry cases.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a cited classification summary rather than a proof reproduced in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Orbifold/log-terminal terminology and exclusions must retain their stated assumptions.

accepted_units.title: A blowup is represented by a quotient action, two charts, and divisibility constraints on equations
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing an exceptional coordinate and quotient action makes both blowup charts explicit; invariance forces powers of the exceptional variable and divisibility conditions that track which deformations survive.
accepted_units.context_note: Concrete point counts are examples; the reusable mechanism is chart equivalence plus invariant equation transformation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: C-star weights, moment-map constraint, summation bounds, and divisibility exponents are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Fiber products, involution quotients, and orbifold bases alter invariants through fixed-locus data
accepted_units.why_material: The examples show how a fiber product or involution quotient builds new threefolds and how fixed curves, resolutions, and quotient singularities control resulting Hodge and base data.
accepted_units.context_note: Treat individual physical models as examples and retain only the generic quotient/fixed-locus dependency.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Tables, involution invariants, and orbifold charts are partially flattened; exact Hodge formulas require verification.

accepted_units.title: Extremal transitions separate contraction type, smoothing availability, and invariant change
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes flops from divisorial contractions, asks whether the contracted singularity admits smoothing, and relates exceptional del Pezzo geometry, root lattices, and Weyl actions to changes across branches.
accepted_units.context_note: Some classification assertions are explicitly not fully verified; retain them as source claims with limits, not settled novelty.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Intersection forms, del Pezzo indices, root counts, and Hodge changes are dense and partly table-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Line-bundle descent gives an arithmetic eligibility test for smoothing contracted curves
accepted_units.why_material: After contracting a negative curve, the coefficient bundles must descend to the singular base; integrality of canonical multiples filters which self-intersections can support an elliptically compatible smoothing.
accepted_units.context_note: The divisibility test is necessary in this setup and does not by itself construct every transition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Signs in adjunction and bundle multiples are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: A transition may require a flop before divisorial contraction and smoothing
accepted_units.why_material: Toric cone data shows that approaching the expected wall first shrinks a curve and produces a flop; only in the adjacent cone can a divisor contract and the singularity be smoothed on a new complex branch. Quotient charts provide an alternative route in another case.
accepted_units.context_note: Connectivity in the enlarged Calabi-Yau moduli space need not imply connectivity inside the elliptically fibered or geometric sublocus.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Weighted-projective coordinates, charge matrices, cone generators, figures, and local singularity equations require exact checking.
